basics.name: Tongze Mao
basics.label: Software Engineer in Test · iOS Developer
basics.summary: Software engineer in test at Veeva Systems, working on Vault infrastructure. Previously built eight Swift apps published on the App Store and two cross-platform Flutter apps for SupTech. Graduated cum laude from UC Irvine with a double major in Computer Science and Informatics and a minor in Statistics. My work connects product design, hands-on development, and careful testing.

work.name: Veeva Systems
work.position: Associate Software Engineer in Test - Infrastructure
work.summary: Test and validate Vault infrastructure across the Durable Queue Framework, FileManager and File Staging API, and Configuration Framework.
highlights: Validate queue isolation, metadata, administration, and upgrade behavior across platform releases.
Help build the queue automation framework, maintain queue automation and triage pipelines, investigate failed runs, and collaborate with the Hyderabad team on continued stability.
Raise design concerns with developers when behavior is ambiguous, difficult to validate, or leaves a failure mode unresolved.
Contribute API and UI automation for Vault Message Isolation, queue metadata, and file staging; investigate automation instability.
Test file staging SDK and API changes, performance enhancements, rate limiting, and remote configuration security changes.
During the Vault Message Isolation rollout, identified critical defects through release validation and contributed to its automation framework while supporting other SET responsibilities.

work.name: SupTech
work.summary: Led development of consumer and technician apps in Flutter and Firebase for a service business.
highlights: Built two cross-platform apps from the initial concept through implementation, covering service requests, scheduling, and order tracking.
Connected the mobile interfaces to backend services, real-time communication, notifications, and payment workflows.
Coordinated development work and worked through interface, integration, and testing issues with the team.

work.name: TZAppify
work.summary: Independent app studio focused on small, practical tools for productivity, learning, and creative work.
highlights: Designed, developed, tested, and published eight Swift apps on the App Store.
DoneTodo reached No. 18 in the App Store Productivity category and appeared in its Top 20 during March, April, and May 2025.
SparkDays reached No. 112 and WayLater No. 169 in the App Store Lifestyle category.
Built interfaces and data models for time planning, calculators, flashcards, habit tracking, writing prompts, and letters to a future self.
Wrote detailed test plans and learned automated testing while developing the apps; debugging became a particular interest.

work.name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
work.position: Research Intern · Dataset Engineering & Stereo 3D Reconstruction
work.summary: Worked on endoscopic stereo-video data preparation for a medical imaging research project.
highlights: Prepared stereo frames and explored disparity estimation and camera-pose extraction with COLMAP.
Reviewed NeRF and point-cloud registration methods and documented the data-processing workflow.

projects.name: Sudoku · Puzzle Engine & Offline Play
projects.summary: Designed and built a bilingual Sudoku PWA with local puzzle generation, saved games, and offline play.
highlights: Implemented bitmask-based MRV backtracking and uniqueness-preserving clue removal, with independent Algorithm X verification.
Built undo and redo that preserve confirmed answers, reversible cell reveals, and statistics that exclude assisted completions.
Built validated local saves and JSON backups, cross-window conflict detection, and versioned service-worker caching.

projects.name: Another Life · Bilingual Life Simulator
projects.summary: Designed and built a life simulation game spanning ten worlds with Next.js, React, and TypeScript.
highlights: Developed a seeded simulation engine with conditional story selection, annual progression, and linked actions within the same year.
Built story graph compilers, causal contracts, and bilingual content checks; added regression tests for choices, timing, and save restoration.
Implemented validated local saves, JSON recovery, offline bilingual play, and optional private cloud backups with serialized writes.

projects.name: SelfVerse · Conversations with Yourself
projects.summary: Designed and built a bilingual web app for user-authored conversations and reflections, with local storage and offline PWA support.
highlights: Created Messages, Moments, and Contacts with perspective-based chat, full-history search, customizable avatars, and 55 illustrated characters.
Implemented transactional IndexedDB persistence, cross-tab synchronization, draft conflict checks, and validated JSON backup and restoration.
Adapted the React and TypeScript interface for desktop and mobile with English and Chinese localization, composition-aware editing, and accessible dialogs.
October 10, 2026 implementation passed 72 unit tests and the production build; added browser coverage for recovery, search, avatars, and large histories.

projects.name: CHROMADAY · Calendar & Structured Notes
projects.summary: Designed and built a minimal calendar with nested daily notes, rich-text editing, and local offline storage.
highlights: Connected month, week, and day views to one structured document model, with expandable outlines, checklists, tables, and a persistent 96-color hierarchy.
Implemented transactional IndexedDB autosave, compare-and-set conflict detection, cross-tab refresh, recoverable drafts, and atomic JSON backup imports.
Built local calendar-date handling, a lazily loaded Tiptap editor, responsive desktop and mobile layouts, and coordinated PWA caching and updates.
October 7, 2026 release verification recorded 169 unit tests, 33 browser tests in each of Chromium and WebKit, and automatic color and background checks.

projects.name: Moment · Web Clock
projects.summary: Designed and built a responsive flip and analog clock as an installable offline PWA.
highlights: Created coordinated flip and SVG analog displays with custom motion, local typography, two themes, and responsive fullscreen layouts.
Implemented shared timestamp calculations, IANA time-zone formatting, server synchronization, and second-boundary scheduling.
Built versioned service-worker caching and coordinated updates; added keyboard controls, reduced-motion support, wake lock, and local preferences.
October 6, 2026 release passed 49 automated tests covering time calculations, offline recovery, update lifecycle, and fullscreen behavior.

projects.name: Humfolio · Musical Idea Notebook
projects.summary: An independent browser application for capturing monophonic humming as editable notes, with A/B audition and MIDI, WAV, and text export.
highlights: Built the React and TypeScript piano roll, Web Audio capture and synthesis, Pitchy-based transcription, and local score storage.
Improved repeated-note segmentation with fine energy boundaries; added recoverable editing and guards against deletion/autosave races.
October 4, 2026 revision passed 52 unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests, including checks against the deployed site.

projects.name: Progress-Tracker API · Time Allocation Backend
projects.summary: A Java/Spring Boot backend for recording and retrieving activity hours.
highlights: Co-developed REST endpoints with typed request mapping, transactional service logic, Spring Data JPA and H2 persistence, and structured JSON error responses.
Added JUnit and Mockito tests and configured Gradle and GitHub Actions for JaCoCo coverage reporting, Checkstyle, and SpotBugs.

projects.name: Taskuadro · Visual Task Planning
projects.summary: An independently developed SwiftUI task board with duration estimates, completion history, and iCloud synchronization.
highlights: Designed Soon, In Progress, Later, and Completed workflows with drag and drop task ordering and manual estimated versus actual duration tracking.
Implemented local JSON persistence, timestamp-based iCloud merging, and completion-date archiving; added XCTest coverage for task operations, ordering, and archive rules.

projects.name: GenClip · Reusable Text Pools
projects.summary: A SwiftUI utility for organizing text pools and copying selected batches to the clipboard.
highlights: Built pool editing with duplicate filtering, live batch previews, and sequential consumption that removes copied items from the remaining pool.
Implemented local Codable JSON persistence with atomic file writes and snapshot-based undo and redo for batch operations.
